A zombie man can get max stat for regen and willpower, but low for resistance, and moderate for stamina (he got exhausted after fighting 1 demon level threat for 10 minutes). 3) heterogenous weighting: from the exams, they seem to make Intelligence and Justice weigh 50% of the exam, and all the other stuff (speed, strength, endurance, fighting ability) to the other 50%. instead if they make all atomic variables weigh equally, the ranking system would be slightly more balanced. 4) they included politics (popularity+achievements)

I remember first watching anime and never skipping fillers; I actually enjoyed them. Outclass != scene stealer. Saitama outclasses everyone, but underpowered guys like licenceless rider still steal scenes. This is true for other anime characters like Rock Lee (everyone loves the underdog... at least he WAS the underdog). however, OPM is different because it cuts everything to the bone; if you remove a scene, there will be diminishment, if you skip an episode and the whole arc collapses. so instead of filler episodes there are filler scenes which take up 90% of the show which is pretty much the same structure as any other show. (I'm not defining fillers as non-canon content, but rather as plot fillers that don't really need filling) Almost all popular shows have these side characters going for them, all anime follow roughly similar character structure:  the rival, the bro from another mo with a slight age difference (Genos... another example: Killer B, Naruto/Klein/Agil, SAO a few others... although these relationship aren't as strong as GenosXsaitama), brother from another mother without an age difference (King...), cool chick (Fubuki), angry chick (Tatsumaki), motivator (metal bat), old guy (bang), the hero (licenceless rider), etc. I would have to disagree and say that OPM season 1 is an excellent gateway to anime, since it's palpable (only 12 episodes), follows roughly the same structure 90% filler, entertaining fillers (there are quite a few in almost all anime), same character roles, smooth transition from mainstream ensemble shows like Monty Python, Seinfeld, HIMYM, and Game of Thrones as well as character focused shows that also emphasizes the background like Breaking Bad, Dr. Who, and Batman the animated series.

If you ever get newly purchased routers direct from the manufacturers, you'll notice the cable is bounded by rubber bands, or some similar constraining object. the circumference of that band would be the band width (it's the width if you cut the band). So unfortunately the maximum bandwidth is predetermined by the manufacturer (if it's a rubber band, then the maximum bandwidth is the length at which the rubber snaps). However a neat trick to increase your bandwidth is to heat the cable with the constraining object in an oven or blowtorch to soften the rubber/plastic which allows you to increase the maximum stretched length. This method is also a great way to lower latency since you can shorten the rubber wires.
